forces.title: Europe leads clean energy and infrastructure adoption
forces.description: Europe, alongside China and North America, is a primary driver of global growth in the power conversion technology market. This leadership stems from its accelerating adoption of clean-energy technologies and ongoing infrastructure upgrades, indicating sustained commitment and investment in the renewable energy and clean tech sector.
forces.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

forces.title: Rapid scale-up of electrolyzer market boosts Green Hydrogen
forces.description: The market for rectifiers in electrolyzer applications, crucial for green hydrogen production, is set for rapid scale-up, projected to grow at 26 percent annually to reach roughly $0.6 billion by 2030. This growth is driven by the necessity for high-power rectifiers to scale electrolyzers to megawatt and gigawatt levels, directly benefiting the green hydrogen segment.
forces.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

forces.title: Accelerating HVDC deployment for offshore wind projects
forces.description: Growth in the HVDC valves market is significantly driven by the accelerating deployment of HVDC systems for offshore wind and urban grid connections. HVDC technology increases efficiency and control for high-power transmission, reduces network losses, and interconnects asynchronous grids, making it crucial for integrating large-scale offshore wind farms into the European grid.
forces.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

forces.title: Market saturation and pricing pressure impact European solar PV
forces.description: The market for power conversion technologies in residential and commercial solar PV in Europe is experiencing contraction, projected to decline by 4 percent annually by 2030. This is attributed to intense pricing pressure and market saturation in mature regions, making competition fierce and potentially hindering new investments in this segment.
forces.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

forces.title: Significant growth in BESS market driven by renewable targets
forces.description: The global Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) power conversion equipment market is expected to triple by 2030, driven by the deployment of utility-scale, grid-connected storage. Europe is projected to experience significant growth due to ambitious renewable-energy targets, addressing increased needs for grid stability, improved capacity utilization, and flexible dispatch as intermittent renewables grow.
forces.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

forces.title: Price compression and competition for utility-scale solar PV
forces.description: The global market for power conversion technologies in utility-scale solar PV is projected to decline by 2 percent through 2030. This contraction is primarily due to significant price compression and increased competition. Compliance with grid codes and grid-stabilizing features will become increasingly important in this challenging market environment.
forces.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

forces.title: Intense price pressure in solar PV and BESS markets
forces.description: Total cost of ownership is a paramount purchasing criterion for customers in both solar photovoltaic and battery energy storage systems markets in Europe and the US. This focus indicates significant price pressure across these segments, which is actively compressing market size despite ongoing demand for clean energy solutions.
forces.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

forces.title: Hybrid AC/DC architecture integration driven by DC-native renewables
forces.description: The energy system is undergoing a structural shift towards hybrid AC/DC architectures. New energy sources like solar PV and batteries are natively DC, and high-density loads such as data centers and EVs consume DC. This necessitates efficient power conversion technologies and a grid that integrates both AC and DC, particularly for behind-the-meter systems and long-distance HVDC transmission, to maximize efficiency and capacity.
forces.source_title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC/DC Power

forces.title: Advancements make DC power viable for renewables integration
forces.description: Technological advancements in power electronics, protection systems, and deployment methods are making direct current (DC) power increasingly viable and cost-effective. Specifically, advances in solid-state and hybrid breakers have largely resolved DC protection challenges. The scaling of power-electronics platforms used in solar inverters and industrial converters continues to narrow the cost differential, facilitating more widespread integration of DC-native renewables and energy storage.
forces.source_title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC/DC Power

forces.title: Growing data center demand creates opportunities for distributed energy
forces.description: The immense and rapidly growing electricity consumption of data centers, combined with extended grid connection waiting times across Europe (up to ten years), creates a significant upside driver for distributed energy resources. The need for efficient, reliable, and swift power solutions for hyperscale campuses incentivizes investment in on-site generation, such as solar, and energy storage, improving overall grid resilience and capacity utilization.
forces.source_title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC/DC Power

forces.title: Increased DC-native integration in commercial buildings
forces.description: Modern commercial buildings are increasingly integrating DC-native components like rooftop solar and battery storage. Live pilots in Lille, France, and Delft, Netherlands, demonstrate that a hybrid DC design consolidates large loads onto a shared backbone, leveraging onsite generation and storage for greater efficiency and reduced peak demand charges. This trend signifies growing adoption and market opportunity for solar and energy storage solutions in the commercial sector.
forces.source_title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC/DC Power

forces.title: Policy and technology shifts for residential solar and batteries
forces.description: Upcoming policy shifts and technological advancements are improving the economic case for residential solar and home batteries. New EU charging point standards (ISO 15118-20 from January 2027) will enable bidirectional power flow, allowing EVs to function as home batteries. Additionally, the increasing prevalence of time-of-use tariffs rewards households for smart electricity usage, enhancing the value of DC-coupled storage by retaining more price advantages.
forces.source_title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC/DC Power

forces.title: Fragmented standards and workforce expertise gap for DC systems
forces.description: Two real barriers to faster adoption of DC-native technologies, which include solar and battery integration, are fragmented standards and a lack of DC-specific workforce expertise. Inconsistent standards across regions increase costs and slow deployment, while the scarcity of engineers and electricians with DC system architecture, protection, and integration capabilities will constrain deployment, similar to early solar PV expansion.
forces.source_title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC/DC Power

forces.title: Irish regulations drive dispatchable generation and storage
forces.description: Since December 2025, Ireland has mandated that every new data center connection must provide dispatchable generation or storage capacity equal to its import capacity. This regulatory requirement acts as a significant tailwind for the energy storage sector, as well as other forms of dispatchable clean energy, by creating guaranteed demand for resilience and flexibility in the Irish energy system.
forces.source_title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC/DC Power

forces.title: Netherlands achieves rapid renewable capacity expansion
forces.description: The Netherlands is identified as one of the countries successfully adding renewable capacity at a faster rate than its demand is rising. This active transition to a low-carbon energy supply in the Netherlands demonstrates strong momentum and favorable conditions for the continued growth and integration of renewable energy projects within the country.
forces.source_title: Investing in the energy transition: Time to look at whole-system value

forces.title: Grid infrastructure lags behind renewable generation build-out
forces.description: The infrastructure required to connect, balance, and secure energy supply, including grids, transmission, storage, and dispatchable backup, remains underfunded and underbuilt. In many major markets, transmission build-out significantly lags behind generation build-out due to long connection queues, complex permitting processes, and supply-chain bottlenecks. This poses a major headwind to the full integration and effectiveness of new renewable energy and energy storage capacity.
forces.source_title: Investing in the energy transition: Time to look at whole-system value

forces.title: Concentrated supply chains pose resilience risk for low-carbon tech
forces.description: The heavy concentration of global supply chains for critical low-carbon technologies, with China supplying over 80 percent of solar modules and 85 percent of battery cell production capacity, poses a significant resilience risk for Europe. This dependency could be even greater than the challenges faced with gas-dependency, potentially impacting the stability and cost-effectiveness of European solar and energy storage deployment.
forces.source_title: Investing in the energy transition: Time to look at whole-system value

forces.title: EU makes progress in reducing emissions
forces.description: Despite global greenhouse gas emissions continuing to rise, the European Union is specifically noted for having made progress in reducing its emissions. This indicates successful policy implementation and investment in decarbonization efforts within the EU, acting as a tailwind for the continued growth and strategic importance of the renewable energy and clean tech sector.
forces.source_title: Investing in the energy transition: Time to look at whole-system value

forces.title: China's massive wind and solar deployment reduces global costs
forces.description: China's extraordinary deployment of wind and solar capacity, including 430 GW installed in 2025 alone, has dramatically reduced the global cost of low-carbon energy technologies. This fierce market competition, coupled with strategic fiscal support, has created a structural change in global pricing, making renewable energy more affordable and accessible for deployment in Europe, despite potential competitive pressures for European manufacturers.
forces.source_title: What the World Can Learn from China’s Energy Transition

viewpoints.title: Slowing growth in renewable energy supply-side applications, but overall market growth
viewpoints.description: While overall demand for power conversion technologies is growing, growth in supply-side applications like renewable energy sources is slowing down. Specifically, the CAGR for solar PV is expected to decline by 2 percent from 2024 to 2030, reflecting market maturation. However, demand-side applications like data centers and EVs are consistently growing at 10 percent or more, ensuring the overall power conversion market's expansion.
viewpoints.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

viewpoints.title: Energy transition not replacing fossil fuels, both growing simultaneously
viewpoints.description: Despite significant global solar capacity growth (30 percent in 2025) and record low-carbon investment, fossil fuels continue to grow in absolute terms, suggesting no direct replacement. The global energy system is building all fuel and power industries in parallel, indicating that the 'peak' for fossil fuels remains elusive. A holistic, system-wide investment perspective is needed to accurately assess the energy transition's true progress beyond mere capacity additions.
viewpoints.source_title: Investing in the energy transition: Time to look at whole-system value

viewpoints.title: Insufficient clean energy investment to reverse rising global emissions
viewpoints.description: Global investment in clean energy, despite making progress in some regions like the European Union, has not yet been sufficient to offset rising energy demand and its associated emissions. Greenhouse gas emissions have continued to increase since the Paris Agreement, highlighting a gap between low-carbon capacity deployment and the necessary scale to bend the global emissions curve downward. A broader investment framework beyond just capacity additions is critical for system performance and resilience.
viewpoints.source_title: Investing in the energy transition: Time to look at whole-system value

viewpoints.title: System optimization needs multi-dimensional balance for energy security
viewpoints.description: Optimizing the energy system solely for cost or emissions reduction is insufficient and creates vulnerabilities. No single energy carrier excels across affordability, reliability, resilience, and emissions reduction. Concentrated supply chains for low-carbon technologies, such as China's dominance in solar modules and battery cells, pose significant resilience risks for Europe, potentially greater than gas dependency. A portfolio approach balancing all four dimensions is crucial for a robust energy transition.
viewpoints.source_title: Investing in the energy transition: Time to look at whole-system value

viewpoints.title: Integrated hybrid power solutions are essential for suppliers to lead
viewpoints.description: Suppliers of power conversion technologies must build integrated portfolios that span capabilities like DC switchgear, battery-integrated DC buses, and energy-management software. The strategic opportunity is to become a systems integrator of hybrid power rather than merely a component supplier, capturing emerging revenue pools in hyperscale AI infrastructure, industrial applications, and eventually commercial/residential buildings. Early market positioning will shape customer expectations and industry economics.
viewpoints.source_title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC/DC Power

viewpoints.title: China's energy transition drivers offer transferable lessons for Europe
viewpoints.description: China's rapid expansion of renewable generation and investment in energy transition supply chains, despite its high absolute emissions, offers valuable lessons. Key drivers like intense market competition, strong innovation, accelerated project delivery, strategic fiscal support, and long-term policy predictability can be adopted by other countries, including those in Europe. Governments need to create durable policy frameworks and strategically use public financing to reduce the cost of energy infrastructure investment.
viewpoints.source_title: What the World Can Learn from China’s Energy Transition

demand_drivers.description: Increasing demand for efficient, reliable power conversion technologies as global mobility, industry, and building systems electrify.
Essential for integrating renewable-energy sources like solar PV and batteries into the grid, as renewables typically produce DC power needing AC conversion.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected global market value in 2030, with a CAGR of 7% from 2024 to 2030. Includes key applications such as utility-scale solar PV technology and energy storage. Derived from McKinsey's Industrials Practice analysis.
market_sizing.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

demand_drivers.description: Electrolyzers require high-power rectifiers to convert AC grid electricity into stable DC current for splitting water molecules, enabling scale-up to megawatt and GW levels.

market_sizing.methodology: Forecasted global market size for rectifiers in electrolyzer applications by 2030, with Europe accounting for roughly 20% of the market. Based on McKinsey Platform for Industrial Electrification.
market_sizing.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

pnl_drivers.description: Intense competition and market saturation in mature regions like Europe are causing pricing pressure, leading to market contraction.

market_sizing.methodology: Expected global market size for power conversion technologies in residential and commercial solar PV by 2030, projected to decline at 4% annually. Europe held 20% of the market in 2025. Based on McKinsey Platform for Industrial Electrification.
market_sizing.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

demand_drivers.description: Major regions are deploying grid-connected storage to support peak shaving, frequency regulation, and renewable energy integration.
Increased energy storage capacity is needed as intermittent power sources (solar, wind) take a larger share of energy supply, especially in Europe and the US.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected global market size for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) power conversion equipment by 2030, expected to triple with an 18% CAGR. Derived from McKinsey Platform for Industrial Electrification.
market_sizing.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

pnl_drivers.description: The market is facing significant price compression and increased competition, leading to a projected decline in value.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected global market size for power conversion technologies in utility-scale solar PV by 2030, with a projected decline of 2% annually. Derived from McKinsey Platform for Industrial Electrification.
market_sizing.source_title: The power conversion market: Decarbonization and growth opportunities

demand_drivers.driver: Global Demand for Energy Transition Technologies
demand_drivers.description: Increased global adoption of renewable energy and clean tech drives demand for components and finished products, leading to significant export growth from major manufacturing hubs.

pnl_drivers.description: Intense competition and strategic fiscal support in China have driven continuous improvements in productivity and accelerated cost reductions, strengthening export competitiveness.

market_sizing.methodology: Value of Chinese exports of energy transition technologies, reaching approximately $147 billion after growing at a compound annual rate of around 18% over the past decade. Major export markets include both the European Union and ASEAN economies. From BCG analysis.
market_sizing.source_title: What the World Can Learn from China’s Energy Transition
